column1: # The frame forms (The frame forms asked, Open 6.4). Each row gives the form of the schema that writes a frame
# relation. It holds the relation as the writer of the vendor passes it back, and the form of the ruleset of the
# schema. It also holds the place in the tuple of the relation that each parameter of that form takes, in the order
# Two rows map the relation exit. The writer uses the row whose places are as many as the text of the form holds.
# That is return where the text holds no guard, and exit_if where it does. The writer writes the predicate relations
# of the ladder the same way, with the test words of the schema. A form that reads the words as signed has `.signed`
# after its relation. The place of the answer is the predicate that the test writes, `where`, and the places of the
# The mirror row of a relation writes the test of the other order from its form, with the places of its words changed
# over. Thus `a <= b` is `b >= a`, and `a < b` is `b > a`. A test that two rows write is one line, from the first of
# its rows that a form answers.
